rebaseCheck: No merge since round 11 (fork point still 1f5b0828). 28d06c20 changes the first start's floor and whoami's event_head (kept marks, event_marks.go), so this was a full round of those paths, plus the regression set.

implementerProof.how: I drove the same surface independently, Dispatch built at 28d06c20 on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of my own, subscribing on /ws/live. Verified: my round-11 red test passes, with its threshold unchanged; with no writer open the first start on 5,000,122 ids takes 44-61 ms; with 3 s writers overlapping it reads no whole log; whoami answers at once with a write open and stays below it; the regression set holds. Rejected because a write from before boot, the case the change addresses, now loses events and makes whoami answer 0 (failures 1 and 2), and because the race lane is red on a hub test this change made time-sensitive (failure 3).

failures.criterion: A page that resumes from whoami's event_head misses nothing and is not replayed the whole log (architect's round-11 item 2, at the case this round's change addresses).
failures.evidence: Red test in b4258ecc634b: TestWhoamiDoesNotSendAPageToReplayTheWholeLogWhileAWriteFromBeforeBootIsOpen in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/routes/whoami_test.go. It fills 1,000 events, opens a write that takes its transaction id before storeRouter registers (and so before the boot mark), ends the write 3 s later, and asks whoami. It fails twice: 'whoami answered event_head 0 while a write from before boot was open, want at least 1000'. It passes with eventFeedHeadWait raised to 5 s (a local edit I reverted, used only as its control). Real surface on 5,000,122 ids (adv.py wboot_whoami head 3): restart while a psql write from before boot is open, then whoami after 2.11 s answered event_head 0, and Dispatch logged 'whoami's event_head is 0, so the page's event feed replays the whole log'. A page resumed from 0 was sent 1,998,016 event frames in its first 120 s and had not reached the newest event, nor the write's own event. Every page that loads after a restart under load, while such a write is open, gets that replay. Round 11's fallback could answer 0 in the same case; I did not test it then.

failures.criterion: Every consumer keeps the order it relies on: a cold subscription is sent every event that commits after it begins (the round-9 contract), on a restart under load.
failures.evidence: Red test in b4258ecc634b: TestTheFirstColdSubscriptionIsSentAnEventCommittedWhileAWriteFromBeforeBootHoldsTheStart in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/live_events_horizon_test.go. It is the implementer's fresh-process test, but the start is held by a write in Dispatch's database that took its id before the boot mark (through testServerOptions.persistence), instead of by a transaction in another database. It fails twice: 'no frame within 30s, waiting for an event of events'. Cause: firstRelayFloor now waits for a mark that counts, and none does until that write ends. The floor is then a mark taken after the write, so every event committed after the subscription began and before the write ended stands at or below the floor, and the subscription starts after it. Real surface (adv.py wboot head, 5,000,122 ids): a write from before boot g=5000211; a comment h=5000212 committed 1 s after the cold subscription; then g committed. events_start said since=5000212, so neither g nor h was ever sent, though both committed after the subscription began. The test passes with round 11's full-read fallback (a local edit I reverted), which fails my round-11 cost test. The two tests together need a start that both waits for that write and finds what committed while it waited without a read from id 0. Inference: today's only /ws/live client, the web app, always resumes from whoami's event_head, so this reaches a cold subscriber only. The contract is documented in feedEvents and in the contracts package.

failures.criterion: CI is green on the head that merges.
failures.evidence: At 28d06c20, envoy-go-race and ci-ok are red; the other 26 lanes are green (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40915071437/job/123603288142). Two causes. (a) internal/dispatch/api: TestADroppedBrokerSubscriptionIsRestoredWithoutMissingAnEvent, 'delivery_live_hub_test.go:1373: no frame within 3s, waiting for a delta of t'. This change made it time-sensitive: the hub's catch-up now waits for the horizon, which any transaction on the instance holds back, and CI's other packages hold transactions on that one Postgres. Locally, with a transaction in database postgres holding an id 4 s of every 4.3 s, it failed 3 of 5 at the head and passed 5 of 5 at main 1f5b0828. It needs a wait that allows for the horizon, as the implementer gave the other hub tests. (b) internal/dispatch/docs hit the lane's 30-minute cap (1800.98 s), with 66 tests reporting 'the test binary's deadline leaves 14 s'. dispatch://INFRA-747 records main's docs package at 1705.9-1745.8 s of that cap under -race. Whether this change added the last minute is unproven.
